title: Quadrium: constructing supply-use and input-output systems, with the measured cost of each assumption
description:
An engine for building and manipulating supply-use and input-output systems: loading published tables from statistical offices, disaggregating sectors against proxy data, balancing with RAS and GRAS, transforming supply-use pairs into symmetric tables, projecting to a later year, regionalising a national table with the location quotient family, estimating how much of a region's trade is two-way with the commodity balance and CHARM, which the quotient family cannot give because a net trade position erases the imports and exports that cancel out, fixing the output of some sectors — a quota, a closure or a capacity — and solving the model for the rest, rather than feeding the change in as demand, which overstates the effect, reporting for each fixed sector the share of its output that others buy as an input because that channel is the one the model cannot see, reading out what a finished table already implies as a table of multipliers — the type I output multiplier and, for any value-added row or satellite account, the direct coefficient, the total effect and total over direct, with the type of multiplier stated on every column and a withheld cell left empty with its reason rather than filled, and loading any region of the European multiregional archive — on its own, or with the rest of its country and the rest of Europe as two further blocks, with Eurostat's regional employment attached.

Every method is implemented against the paragraph and page of the manual that specifies it, and verified against that manual's own printed numbers. Every cell carries whether it was observed, estimated from a proxy or moved by the balancer, and that status survives the file boundary. Every result is printed together with the measured cost of the assumptions that produced it — figures obtained by running each method against tables where the answer is independently known. What the sources get wrong is measured too, and stated rather than repaired in silence: nineteen region labels of the European archive name another region and are corrected on load, neither of its accounting identities closes and the residue is carried in sight, and against ten surveyed regions it records about a quarter of the purchases a region makes from the rest of its country.

The data files distributed with the software are official statistics published by Eurostat, the UK Office for National Statistics, the Spanish INE and the United Nations Statistics Division, each under its own reuse terms, together with the European multiregional archive of Huang and Koutroumpis (2023, CC BY 4.0); see PROVENANCE.md. The MIT licence covers the software only.
